[[ ## thread ## ]]
From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Depreciation treatment for new CNC machine purchase

Gabriel,

We are finalizing the acquisition of a new CNC machining center (PO #45821, ~$420k with installation). Before we close, I need your read on the proper depreciation treatment under current tax rules — specifically whether we should be looking at MACRS (and which class life) or if Section 179 / bonus depreciation is the better route for our situation.

We want to make sure we're optimizing cash flow for FY25, and I'd like a clear recommendation we can take to our tax preparer. If you need the asset details or invoice breakdown, I can send them over.

Also, Victor — flagging you for visibility since this ties into our Q3 capex forecast.

Thanks,
Dana Whitfield
Controller, Kestrel Manufacturing

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Depreciation treatment for new CNC machine purchase

Hi Dana,

Thanks for looping me in on this. Based on the details you've shared (PO #45821, ~$420k including installation), here's my read:

For a CNC machining center used in manufacturing, MACRS generally applies as 7-year property. Under current rules, you have two main options to consider:

1. **Section 179**: You can expense up to the annual limit (well above $420k for FY25), which would let you deduct the full purchase price in the year placed in service, subject to the business income limit. This gives you the fastest cash-flow benefit if you have sufficient taxable income.

2. **Bonus depreciation**: If you don't want to use Section 179 or want to preserve some basis, bonus depreciation (currently 80% for property placed in service in 2024) can be applied to the remaining balance, with the rest depreciated over the 7-year MACRS schedule.

For your situation, assuming Kestrel has profitable operations and can use the full deduction, **Section 179 is likely the better route** — it allows you to write off the entire $420k in FY25, maximizing cash flow. If you prefer to spread the deduction or anticipate income limitations, bonus depreciation plus regular MACRS is a solid fallback.

One note: installation costs are typically included in the depreciable basis, so your ~$420k figure should be the right starting point. I'd recommend confirming with your tax preparer, but this gives you a clear direction to take them.

If you want, I can pull together a simple side-by-side cash-flow comparison for FY25 under both scenarios — just let me know. Happy to send the asset details or invoice breakdown if you need them from my side.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Re: Depreciation treatment for new CNC machine purchase

Gabriel,

Thanks for the quick and clear rundown. That aligns with what I suspected — Section 179 for the full $420k is the way to go if we can use it against income, and our taxable income for FY25 should comfortably cover that. I'll take your recommendation to our preparer as the primary path, with bonus depreciation as the fallback if anything changes on the income side.

Appreciate the note on installation costs being included in basis — that's how I had it booked, so good to have confirmation.

One follow-up: yes, a side-by-side cash-flow comparison for FY25 under both scenarios would be useful. Send it over when you can — I'll use it in our board packet.

Victor, just so you know where this lands — the full expensing route helps our FY25 cash position, which should ease some pressure on the Q3 capex forecast. Happy to walk through the numbers if needed.

Thanks,
Dana Whitfield
Controller, Kestrel Manufacturing
